Hashing: Compute cryptographic digests of values, lists, and entire datasets. Supports BLAKE3, BLAKE2b / BLAKE2s, the SHA-2 / SHA-3 families, SHAKE128 / SHAKE256 with any output length, Ethereum's Keccak, RIPEMD-160 and SM3, plus legacy MD5 / SHA-1 for compatibility. The aggregate variant produces an order-deterministic dataset checksum.
HMAC: Keyed message authentication codes and constant-time comparison. Use for signing API requests, verifying message integrity, or building tamper-evident audit trails — anywhere a hash needs a shared secret.
Random: Cryptographically secure random bytes from OpenSSL's CSPRNG. Use for encryption keys, salts, nonces, and any other cryptographic material that must be unpredictable.
Key Derivation: Password hashing and key derivation with Argon2, scrypt, PBKDF2 and HKDF. Use Argon2 or scrypt to store passwords, and HKDF to derive several keys from one high-entropy secret.
